reasoning: The package sources from a pinned GitHub tag (v0.6.0) with SHA-256 checksum verification, uses standard Rust/cargo build process, and has conventional installation steps (copy binary, assets, desktop file, license, create symlink). No evidence of code injection, no execution of fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts. The only disagreement was caused by a tool error in one model, not by substantive security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) during the full PKGBUILD review, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. This is a tool failure, not a substantive disagreement about security.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures) should be handled gracefully - the initial PKGBUILD audit succeeded for qwen but the full review failed, creating an inconclusive result when the package was actually safe
When one model has a tool error and another successfully reviews all files, the successful review should carry the verdict rather than defaulting to inconclusive
Standard Rust/cargo packaging patterns are well-understood by models and don't require additional scrutiny when checksums are pinned
